spans.title: The Man Who Wouldn't Fight
spans.blurb: A traveler in a grey tweed suit endures a carriage of strangers' contempt for not being at the front, while hiding the reason he cannot answer them.

spans.title: Escape by Aeroplane
spans.blurb: A fugitive slips into the air in a friend's aeroplane just ahead of the police, tastes the pure joy of flight, then the engine begins to sputter.

spans.title: Taken for an Informer
spans.blurb: A gentleman who notes down everything takes a cab across London, and his notebook convinces the driver of something sinister enough to start a street brawl.
spans.brokenNote: The final sentence is cut off mid-phrase, so the passage ends on an unfinished clause even though the comic arc itself is complete.

spans.title: The Lady at the Window
spans.blurb: A visitor enters a breakfast room and sees a graceful stranger at the far window; each step she takes toward him revises what he thinks he sees.

spans.title: A Touch at Midnight
spans.blurb: On a lonely road at one in the morning, a hand falls on a walker's shoulder, and a woman dressed all in white asks the way to London.

spans.title: The Duel in Hunter's Bog
spans.blurb: A leering stranger picks a quarrel, blow answers insult, and a young man who has never learned to fence must walk to a duel he expects to lose.

spans.title: The Bowl of Rack Punch
spans.blurb: At a pleasure garden, one bowl of punch proves too tempting for a vain gourmand, and an evening that should have settled a marriage goes gloriously sideways.

spans.title: Treated Like a Fly
spans.blurb: A man sunk in depression walks into a tavern half hoping to be thrown out of a window, and receives an insult far harder to forgive.

spans.title: Look at the Sheets
spans.blurb: A whispered warning from the woodman's wife sends a traveler to check his bed, and what he finds keeps him listening in the dark at the window.

spans.title: Asking for More
spans.blurb: In a workhouse where boys starve on thin gruel, lots are cast, and one small desperate child must walk up to the master and ask for more.

spans.title: A Word Against His Mother
spans.blurb: A charity-boy bully needles a quiet orphan at dinner, prodding and jeering until he finds the one subject that turns the mild child to fire.

spans.title: His Formidable Aunt
spans.blurb: A boy who has walked for days, robbed and sleeping in fields, gathers his last courage to introduce himself to an aunt famous for chasing boys away.
spans.spoilerNote: It reveals that the narrator's mother has died, a loss the full book only reaches after several chapters.

spans.title: Let Me In
spans.blurb: Kept awake by a branch tapping the glass, a sleeper breaks the pane to silence it, and his fingers close on something that grips back.

spans.title: The Lighted Window
spans.blurb: Two wild children run barefoot through the dark to spy on a rich family's bright window, laughing at what they see, until the bulldog is let loose.
